system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Executive view

The Seller’s package departs from several express Wattlebridge positions and should not be accepted as a balanced package. The principal pushbacks are the reduced general cap and claim thresholds; the proposed collapse of fundamental/title claims into the general regime; the broad disclosure, knowledge and all-claims limitations; and inadequate Bluefen and Riverlark completion protections. There are also unresolved completion-funds, IP, incident, supplier-renewal and title-evidence issues.

No written authority has been given for the playbook’s conditional fallbacks. Accordingly, retain the **25% / AUD 6 million general cap** and **24-month general claim period** as the positions to mark up; do not offer the **20% / AUD 4.8 million cap** or **18 months** without Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the draft.

## Material departures and recommended pushbacks

| Issue | Seller position / disclosure | Buyer position and recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| **General warranty cap** | 20% of price, or AUD 4.8 million. | Restore the **25% / AUD 6 million** starting position. The Seller’s figure is an unapproved conditional fallback, not an agreed position. |
| **De minimis and basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, with only the excess recoverable. | Restore **AUD 5,000 de minimis** and **AUD 50,000 aggregate basket**, with the Seller liable **from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded**. The proposed thresholds materially reduce the claims that can be pursued and add a tipping-point reduction in recovery. |
| **General claim period** | 18 months; proposal that limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | Require **24 months after Completion** for general warranty claims. Eighteen months is an unapproved fallback. Draft the general time limit so it does not silently govern other claim categories. |
| **Fundamental and title claims** | Same caps and time limits as general warranties. | Reject. Provide a **separate regime** for fundamental/title claims, with a **100% cap and at least six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. |
| **Fraud and deliberate misconduct** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature. | Carve **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct** out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is a non-waivable playbook position. Do not rely on a general “unless expressly stated” formulation to protect it. |
| **Disclosure standard** | General disclosure of the indexed data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records; specific disclosures are also made. | Reject deemed disclosure of the entire data room, public registers or matters discoverable through a prudent search. Require **specific, fair disclosure** against the relevant warranty. The letter itself says the general disclosure sweeps in DD-002 to DD-012, while its reservation does not establish that those materials fairly disclose every relevant matter. |
| **Buyer knowledge** | No claim for anything known by Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion. If any knowledge qualifier is retained, limit it to identified Seller knowledge persons following reasonable enquiry; it must never qualify title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Knowledge should not be imputed simply because information was in the data room or public records. |
| **Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. | Require **effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion**. Consent on delivery alone is insufficient if conditions remain outstanding. Reasonable endeavours alone is inadequate for a material customer: DD-002 records about AUD 3.6 million FY26 revenue (approximately 30%) and the consent conditions. The letter confirms that neither final consent nor evidence of satisfied conditions is included. Make this a properly satisfied completion condition, not merely an efforts covenant. |
| **Riverlark debt and security** | Approximately AUD 3.2 million outstanding; release to follow Completion. | Require a **current payout**, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-Completion release is not acceptable without an **irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval**. DD-003 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no final discharge is included. |
| **DD-005 bonuses and funds flow** | AUD 420,000 bonuses are “a matter for the Seller,” but are not separately itemised. | Require the bonuses, plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs, to be a **specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded**. Do not permit a silent omission or leave responsibility unclear. The disclosure confirms the bonuses are conditional, absent from the draft funds flow, and that on-costs are unstated. Clarify who pays even if the conditions are not ultimately triggered. |
| **Ironquay IP** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller calls it adequate. | Broaden the indemnity to address the **transfer and ownership/availability of relevant Ironquay IP and Project Materials**, including the consequences of missing rights or transfer, while preserving the **SOW3 cure**. DD-004 says transfer is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open but is not independent bank verification. The room contains neither a payment receipt nor confirmatory assignment. Do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently established as either paid or unpaid. |
| **DD-006 export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material. | Do not accept a dismissive materiality conclusion or assert an established breach. The disclosure says the link went to an unintended external email, may contain about 1,240 records, and access, scope and notification obligations remain unknown. Require **preservation of logs, a proper investigation and continuing updates**, with appropriate contractual protection for any resulting breach or liability. On this record, assume **no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand**, in either direction. |
| **Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess their timing, scope and contractual status; do **not** accept automatic Debt classification or a price deduction. DD-008 and DD-011 are to be read together and record AUD 330,000 aggregate, but the letter does not establish whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Seek the underlying terms and apply the agreed price mechanics, not an unsupported label. |
| **Title evidence** | DD-012 share register is said to evidence title to 100% of the shares. | Require **independent evidence** of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal source; the letter expressly does not say the Buyer completed independent verification. Do not treat the register alone as conclusive proof. |
| **Tax and IP warranty positions** | Seller says these are settled under the general regime. | They remain **open** under the playbook. Do not accept their incorporation into the general regime, or infer unlimited liability or a resolution. Keep Tax, IP and other claim categories separately defined and negotiated. |
| **Other contract notices/consents** | Disclosure identifies an office-lease notification obligation and a Mossvale assignment restriction. | Check the full documents and completion requirements. The letter does not establish that landlord consent is required for the share sale or that Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold. Do not elevate either into a consent requirement without contractual support, but do confirm any actual notice or consent obligations are met. |

## Drafting approach

Insist that the SPA keep **Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant** claims distinct from the general warranty regime. In particular, review the interaction of clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 with the claim-specific provisions: a general limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause must not override the negotiated treatment of another category or the mandatory fraud/misconduct carve-out.

The Disclosure Letter’s broad general-disclosure wording should be replaced or qualified so that only specifically and fairly disclosed matters qualify the relevant warranties. Its statements that it does not admit breach, liability, materiality or legal requirements are reservations, not resolution of the underlying DD issues.

## Summary recommendations

1. Restore the **25% / AUD 6 million cap**, **AUD 5,000 de minimis**, **AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, and **24-month general claims period**; seek written Amelia Frost approval before using either stated fallback.
2. Establish a separate **100% / at least six-year** regime for fundamental/title claims, and preserve the non-waivable fraud, wilful-concealment and deliberate-misconduct carve-out.
3. Reject blanket data-room/public-register disclosure and Buyer-knowledge exclusions; require specific fair disclosure and tightly controlled knowledge wording.
4. Make Bluefen’s effective consent **and satisfaction of conditions** a Completion requirement; repay Riverlark directly from Completion funds and obtain effective releases, subject only to the stated approved-undertaking exception.
5. Resolve the bonus funding and on-costs in the funds flow; broaden the Ironquay protection while preserving the SOW3 cure.
6. Require DD-006 investigation, log preservation and updates; assess Sandbar without automatic debt treatment; and obtain independent title evidence.
7. Keep Tax and IP open and all claim categories clearly separated.
=== END ADVICE ===
